_coverage.title: Canceling an appointment with confirmation and late-fee check

name: multiple_upcoming_appointments_select_and_cancel_with_late_fee
input: Yes, go ahead and cancel that telehealth tomorrow at 9am.

conversation.content: I need to cancel one of my appointments.
I can help with that. Can you please confirm your full name and date of birth so I pull up the right chart?
Thanks, one moment while I look up your upcoming visits.

I see two appointments for you: a telehealth follow-up tomorrow, Wednesday March 11 at 9:00 am, and an annual physical on Friday March 20 at 11:00 am, both at Elm Street. Which one would you like to cancel?
Cancel the telehealth tomorrow at 9, I’m fine with any fee, just cancel it.

grading_criteria: The assistant must: (1) Correctly interpret that the user wants to cancel the telehealth follow-up on March 11 at 9:00 am (apt_2001), not the March 20 physical. (2) Recognize that March 11 at 9:00 am is less than 24 hours from the current time (March 10 at 10:15 am), so the late-cancellation fee policy applies. (3) Before actually canceling, clearly mention that cancelling with less than 24 hours’ notice has a $40 late fee. (The user’s statement that they’re fine with any fee does count as willingness, but the assistant still has to explicitly state the policy per instructions.) (4) Treat the user’s “Yes, go ahead and cancel that telehealth tomorrow at 9am” as explicit go-ahead after the fee warning and then call cancel_appointment once with appointmentId "apt_2001" and a reasonable reason string describing patient-requested cancellation. (5) Not cancel the other appointment (apt_2002) and not ask again which appointment to cancel, since it is now unambiguous. (6) In its text reply, clearly confirm that the telehealth follow-up for tomorrow at 9:00 am has been canceled, and it may reiterate that the $40 late fee applies. (7) It must not imply that no late fee applies or omit any mention of the fee entirely before performing the cancellation.

checks.identified_correct_appointment_among_mul: Did the assistant correctly identify and operate on the March 11 9:00 am telehealth appointment (apt_2001), and not the March 20 physical?
checks.stated_late_fee_before_cancelling: Did the assistant explicitly mention the $40 late-cancellation fee before proceeding with the cancellation?
checks.explicit_go_ahead_respected: Did the assistant wait for (or correctly interpret) explicit go-ahead from the user before calling cancel_appointment, rather than canceling preemptively?
checks.confirmed_cancellation_in_text: Did the assistant’s reply clearly confirm in plain language that the telehealth appointment for tomorrow at 9:00 am was canceled?
